# Churchill Downs News Release: Former Trainer David Vance Passes Away at 86


## Nov 25, 2026


David Vance, who trained champion Caressing and won four Churchill Downs training titles during a 58-year career, has died. He was 86.


Vance retired in July 2023 with 3,193 victories, according to Equibase, including a documented 380 at Churchill Downs.


His best-known runner was longtime owner Carl Pollard’s Caressing, the champion 2-year-old filly of 2000. With John Velazquez aboard, Caressing upset the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies (GI) at Churchill Downs at odds of 47-1.


Vance also trained Pollard’s My Trusty Cat, winner of the 2005 Humana Distaff (GI) at Churchill Downs, and graded stakes winners Kiss Moon and her dam, Kiss the Devil. Both Kiss Moon and Kiss the Devil won the Mint Julep (GIII) beneath the Twin Spires.


“David Vance devoted his life to horse racing and built a career that included four Churchill Downs training titles and numerous graded stakes victories,” said Churchill Downs Racetrack President Mike Anderson. “He took great pride in seeing his children share that same passion through their own involvement in the sport. Our thoughts are with the entire Vance family during this difficult time.”


Vance rode as a teenager and was among the leading jockeys at the now-closed Thunderbird Downs in Las Vegas during the 1950s. He later assisted his father, Richard, before opening his own stable in 1965.


His first Churchill Downs training title came at the 1967 Spring Meet. He added Spring Meet titles in 1980 and 1981 and the 1994 Fall Meet championship, along with multiple titles at Garden State Park, Keystone Park and Oaklawn Park.


Survivors include his wife, Lynn, and children Tommy, Travis and Tricia.
